title: Layers, UI, masks and zoom views
summary: Separate world and screen layouts, control visibility with masks, and compose multiple views.

blocks.text: An entity is visible to a camera when `(entity.layerMask & camera.cullingMask) !== 0`, subject to other visibility/culling conditions. Entities default to layer zero; UI reserves layer 31. Use layer helpers rather than manually shifting bits when readable code matters. Parent/child inheritance and explicit flags still affect traversal.

RenderView combines a camera, viewport and target. Scenes share the composer’s view collection. Use independent cameras for split views, offscreen passes and UI, then select content with masks. UIManager creates an orthographic screen-space view when UI entities are detected. isUI and layer membership are different properties that work together.

Mask wraps a VectorEntity shape and content, with optional inversion. The stencil pipeline uses depth24plus-stencil8 and specialized mask passes. Mask IDs use the lower seven stencil bits and wrap after 127; bit 7 is also used by analytical path filling. Stencil behavior depends on the content’s renderer. Analytical Path content and fast-path mega batching need explicit verification; the example below uses a text mask with a Sprite. Entity.scissorClipRect is the rectangular clipping property, with different semantics from arbitrary vector masking.

ZoomView renders target content through a dedicated view and window, optionally with connectors. FeedbackZoomView samples frame feedback. The feedback alternative is useful for lower-cost insets but represents a prior captured frame and inherits feedback lifetime constraints. Choose by whether the inset needs its own fresh scene rendering or an image of the existing output.
